svg.title: Naming every guess you had to make about the original engine
svg.desc: Reimplementing an engine means guessing at behaviour nobody documented. Each guess is written down and given an identifier — how whitespace in a name is handled, whether matching is case sensitive, what a sentinel value means, which timezone a time-of-day rule uses, how weights are normalised, what happens when nothing matches, whether rule order matters, how a disabled flag behaves. When a replayed decision diverges, it is automatically tagged with the assumptions that could explain it, so a divergence points at a specific guess rather than at the whole system. Some assumptions have been settled by observed divergences. The rest remain open and are declared as open.
svg.text: Every guess about undocumented behaviour, written down
Whitespace inside a name — trimmed, or significant?
A field that is not quite a boolean — what counts as true?
A negative sentinel value — missing, or genuinely negative?
Which timezone does a time-of-day rule use?
How are weights normalised across candidates?
What happens when nothing matches at all?
Does the order rules appear in change the outcome?
A divergence is auto-tagged with the assumptions that could explain it,
so a failure points at one named guess rather than at the whole rewrite.
